Board Important – Karnataka 2nd PUC Blueprint

Chapter-wise weightage, the highest-yield topics, and the exact answers examiners look for in Evolution — also one of the most heavily tested chapters in NEET and KCET.
~7–9 marksConsistently one of the highest-weightage chapters in the 2nd PUC Biology paper
1 × 5 MUsually one long answer – Miller-Urey experiment, Darwin's theory of natural selection, or origin & evolution of man
1–2 × 3 MEvidences of evolution, Hardy-Weinberg principle (with numerical), types of natural selection
2–3 × 2 MHomologous vs analogous organs, Lamarckism vs Darwinism, adaptive radiation examples
1–2 × 1 MDefinitions and scientists – Oparin-Haldane, de Vries, founder effect, biogenetic law
Board Important — Repeated Question Bank
Categorized model answers and value points for the most-repeated board questions.

⭐⭐⭐ Top priority – almost always asked

  • Miller-Urey experiment (5 M) – draw the spark-discharge apparatus; label the flask with CH4, NH3, H2 in 2:1:2 ratio, the boiling-water flask, the electrodes (simulating lightning at ~800°C) and the condenser/trap. State the observation – amino acids and simple organic compounds (HCN, fatty acids, urea) were formed – and the inference that chemical evolution of life is possible.
  • Darwin's theory of natural selection (5 M) – state the postulates in order: overproduction, limited resources, struggle for existence, variation, survival of the fittest (Herbert Spencer)/natural selection (Darwin), inheritance of useful variations, formation of new species. Mention Malthus's influence and On the Origin of Species (1859).
  • Origin and evolution of man (5 M) – sequence: Dryopithecus/Ramapithecus → Australopithecus (Homo habilis, 2 mya) → Homo erectus (Java man, Peking man; 1.5 mya, ~900cc) → Homo neanderthalensis (1,00,000–40,000 yrs, 1400cc) → Homo sapiens (modern man). Give brain capacities and key discoverers.
  • Evidences of evolution (5 M) – paleontological (fossils), embryological (biogenetic law), morphological/anatomical (homologous vs analogous organs with examples), biochemical, and biogeographical (Darwin's finches, Australian marsupials).
  • Hardy-Weinberg principle (5 M) – state p + q = 1 and p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1; explain genetic equilibrium and the five disturbing factors (gene migration, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, natural selection). Be ready to solve a numerical.

⭐⭐ High priority – frequently asked

  • Theories of origin of life (3 M) – Special Creation (Father Suarez), Cosmozoic/Panspermia (Hermann Richter), Abiogenesis (Aristotle), Biogenesis (Redi, Spallanzani, Pasteur's swan-neck flask) – know who disproved whom and why.
  • Chemical evolution of life – Oparin-Haldane theory (3 M) – reducing atmosphere, formation of simple → complex organic molecules, coacervates (Oparin) and microspheres (Sydney Fox) as protobiont models.
  • Lamarckism (3 M) – principles (influence of environment, use and disuse of organs, inheritance of acquired characters), giraffe-neck example, and Weismann's decaudalisation experiment (22 generations, tail-less rats still produced tailed progeny) that disproved it. Germplasm theory as its corollary.
  • Types of natural selection (3 M) – stabilizing (plant height), directional (adaptive melanism / peppered moth), disruptive (rabbit fur colour) – draw the three bell-curve diagrams.
  • Adaptive radiation (3 M) – Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands (beak variation by diet) and Australian marsupials (radiating from a single ancestral stock); convergent evolution of placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf.
  • Mutation theory of Hugo de Vries (2–3 M) – work on Oenothera lamarckiana (evening primrose), saltation (single-step large mutation), and the comparison table: Darwinian variation (minor, directional, gradual) vs mutation (large, random, saltatory).

⭐ Two-mark favourites – learn as clean pairs

  • Homologous organs vs analogous organs · divergent evolution vs convergent evolution.
  • Big Bang theory (Lemaitre) vs Nebular theory (Kant) · Abiogenesis vs Biogenesis.
  • Lamarckism vs Darwinism · Darwinian variation vs mutation (de Vries).
  • Adaptive melanism as directional selection · founder effect (bottleneck/Sewall Wright effect).
  • Coacervate theory (Oparin) vs microsphere theory (Sydney Fox) · biogenetic law (Haeckel) – disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer.
Answer-writing tip: for every 5-mark experiment, the examiner expects five numbered points – the apparatus/material, the treatment/procedure, the observation, any control, and the conclusion. Write them as (i)–(v), not as a paragraph.
Never lose these marks: always write the scientist and the year – Lemaitre 1927, Kant 1755, Redi 1688, Spallanzani 1765, Oparin 1924/1938, Sydney Fox 1959, Miller-Urey 1953, Darwin 1859, Weismann's experiment, Hugo de Vries 1901, Hardy & Weinberg 1908.

Important Diagrams

📖 Every high-yield figure in this chapter, ranked by board-exam priority with its typical mark weightage and the exact labels you must show — so you always know which diagrams matter most.
Evolution — Important Diagrams & Marks Guide
Board-exam priority list of key diagrams with mark weightage, crucial labels and marking scheme notes.

Origin of Universe & Earth

Fig 6.1 — Big Bang & Formation of Galaxies 1 – 2 M ★★☆ High Priority
Show the single titanic explosion (~15 billion years ago), expansion & cooling, formation of Hydrogen & Helium, and condensation into galaxies. Label George Lemaitre as proposer (1927).
Fig 6.2 — Nebular Theory of Origin of Earth 1 M ★☆☆ Occasional
Label the rotating nebula, its explosion into nebulae, heavier elements (Fe, Ni) sinking to form the core, lighter elements (Si, Al) forming the crust, and the lightest (H, He, N, O) forming the atmosphere. Proposed by Immanuel Kant (1755).

Theories of Origin of Life

Fig 6.3 — Redi's & Pasteur's Experiments (Biogenesis) 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw Redi's covered vs open meat jars (no maggots in covered jars). Draw Pasteur's S-necked (swan-neck) flask – broth stays uncontaminated because dust & microbes are trapped in the curved neck, disproving spontaneous generation.
Fig 6.4 — Miller-Urey Spark Discharge Apparatus 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: flask with CH4, NH3, H2 (2:1:2) and water vapour; the boiling water flask (simulating ocean); the spark-discharge electrodes (simulating lightning, ~800°C); the condenser; and the trap where amino acids collected.

Evidences of Evolution

Fig 6.5 — Homologous Forelimbs of Mammals 2 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw the forelimb bones of man, bat, cheetah and whale side by side – same basic bone arrangement (humerus, radius-ulna, carpals) but different external form/function. Label as homology → divergent evolution.
Fig 6.6 — Archaeopteryx – the Connecting Link 2 M ★★☆ High Priority
Label reptilian features (teeth, clawed free fingers, long unfused tail vertebrae) and avian features (feathers, beak-like jaws) on the same fossil sketch, showing it as the connecting link between reptiles and birds.
Fig 6.7 — Industrial Melanism in Biston betularia 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Two panels: light-lichen-covered tree trunk (white moths camouflaged, dark moths eaten) before industrialisation; soot-blackened trunk (dark moths camouflaged, white moths eaten) after industrialisation.

Biogeographical Evidence & Natural Selection

Fig 6.8 — Darwin's Finches (Adaptive Radiation) 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Sketch several finch species radiating from a common ancestral seed-eater, with beaks shaped differently for seed-crushing, insect-picking and cactus-probing diets, all on the Galapagos Islands.
Fig 6.9 — Three Types of Natural Selection 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw three bell curves side by side: stabilizing (peak in the middle rises, both tails shrink – plant height), directional (whole peak shifts one way – adaptive melanism), disruptive (middle sinks, both tails rise – rabbit fur colour).

Origin & Evolution of Man

Fig 6.10 — Stages in Human Evolution 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw the progression of skulls/figures with increasing brain capacity and erect posture: Dryopithecus → Australopithecus (~500–700cc) → Homo habilis (~650–800cc) → Homo erectus (~900cc) → Homo neanderthalensis (~1400cc) → Homo sapiens (~1450cc). Label age and cranial capacity for each stage.

Chapter 6 – Mind Map

One-page visual overview of the whole chapter · pinch or use buttons to zoom
EVOLUTION
1 · ORIGIN OF UNIVERSE & EARTH
Big Bang (Lemaitre, 1927) · ~15 billion years ago
Nebular theory (Kant, 1755) · earth ~4.5 billion years old
Early atmosphere: H2O, CH4, CO2, NH3
UV split water → O2 escaped · ozone layer formed
Life appeared ~500 million years after earth formed (~4 bya)
2 · THEORIES OF ORIGIN OF LIFE
Special Creation (Father Suarez) · Cosmozoic/Panspermia (Richter)
Abiogenesis (Aristotle, spontaneous generation)
Biogenesis (Redi 1688 → Spallanzani 1765 → Pasteur, swan-neck flask)
Pasteur disproved abiogenesis once and for all
3 · CHEMICAL EVOLUTION OF LIFE
Oparin (1924) & Haldane · reducing atmosphere
Inorganic → simple organic → macromolecules → protobiont
Coacervates (Oparin, 1938) · Microspheres (Sydney Fox, 1959)
Miller-Urey (1953): CH4:NH3:H2 = 2:1:2, spark discharge → amino acids
4 · EVIDENCES OF EVOLUTION
Paleontological (fossils, radioactive dating)
Embryological (biogenetic law – Haeckel; disproved by von Baer)
Morphological: homologous (divergent) vs analogous (convergent)
Biochemical (proteins, genes) · Biogeographical (finches, marsupials)
Natural selection in action: adaptive/industrial melanism
5 · LAMARCKISM
Jean Baptist Lamarck, Philosophie Zoologique (1809)
Use & disuse of organs · inheritance of acquired characters
Giraffe neck (use) · snake limblessness (disuse)
Disproved: Weismann's decaudalisation (22 generations)
Germplasm theory (Weismann): somatoplasm vs germplasm
6 · DARWINISM & NATURAL SELECTION
Darwin + Wallace · H.M.S. Beagle · Origin of Species (1859)
Overproduction → struggle → variation → survival of fittest (Spencer)
Malthus's population essay influenced Darwin
Types: stabilizing, directional, disruptive selection
Criticism: doesn't explain vestigial organs, arrival of fittest
7 · MUTATION THEORY & HARDY-WEINBERG
Hugo de Vries (1901) · Oenothera lamarckiana · saltation
Mutation: large, random, sudden vs Darwinian: small, directional
H-W: p + q = 1, p2+2pq+q2=1 (genetic equilibrium)
Disturbed by: migration, drift, mutation, recombination, selection
Founder effect = bottleneck / Sewall Wright effect
8 · ORIGIN & EVOLUTION OF MAN
Dryopithecus & Ramapithecus (~15 mya)
Australopithecus (~2 mya, 500–700cc, Lucy)
Homo habilis (650–800cc) → Homo erectus (~900cc, Java/Peking man)
Homo neanderthalensis (1400cc) → Homo sapiens (modern man)
Cro-Magnon man – most recent direct ancestor
